1. Scope — Covers buffer bands for cop-changing automatic looms. 

2. Materials 

2.1 Tanned Ox or Buffalo Hide — The degree of tanning, determined as prescribed in LC:21 of 
IS : 582-1970 • Methods for chemical testing of leathers ( first revision ) ', shall be not less than 55% 

2.2 Rivets — Countersunk head type [see also IS: 2155-1962 'Specification for rivets for general 
purposes ( below 12 mm diameter) ' ]. 

2.3 Washers — See IS : 2016-1967 ' Specification for plain washers ( first revision ) \ 

3. Shape, Dimensions and Workmanship — Generally as shown in Fig. 1. It shall be provided 
with two runners, loose or riveted as specified in the contract

SECTION XX 



All dimensions in millimetres. 

Note 1— inner dimensions of major and minor axis shall be measured after mounting the buffer band in a 
suitable measuring block. 

Note 2 — The runners may have the curvature of runner fit at the option of the buyer. 

Note 3 — The total length of runner when mounted shall not be less than 83 mm including a clearance of 2 mm 
( as detailed at Section XX ). 

FIG. 1 TYPICAL BUFFER BAND FOR COP-CHANGING AUTOMATIC LOOMS 

3.1 Substance ( or Thickness) — When tested in accordance with LP : 1 of IS : 5914-1970 f Methods 
of physical testing of leather ', the thickness shall be 9'0 ± 0'5 mm at any part of the buffer band. 

3-2 Layers — Two layers firmly cemented, each 4"5 ± 0'5 mm thick. 

4. Splices in the Joint — Cemented, not less than 10 cm long and trimmed to a fine angle. 



Adopted 29 October 1976

INDIAN STANDARDS INSTITUTION

IS: 1619- 1976 

4-1 For the purpose of jointing, a good quality cellulose or synthetic resin cement shall be used to 
ensure a waterproof and flexible Joint. 

4.2 When the jointed portion of the buffer band is bent to an angle of 90° over an iron form of 5 cm 
in diameter, the splices shall not open at the ends of the joint. 

4.3 The buffer band shall have preferably one ( or maximum two ) joints. 

5. Tensile Strength and Elongation — When at least 5 buffer bands in a sample selected at 
random from a lot are tested in accordance with LP : 6 of IS : 5914-1970: 

a) the average tensile strength shall not be less than 210 kgf* per cm width, and 

b) the average elongation shall not exceed 6 percent at a load of 50 kgf/cm 2 cross-sectional 
area applied for 15 minutes. 

6. Packing — Unless otherwise specified, the buffer band shall be wrapped in waterproof paper 
and then packed in suitable containers. 

7. Marking — The packages shall bear information regarding name of product and the quantity 
packed, manufacturers ' name and trade-mark; and the month and year of manufacture. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking Scheme — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 



*1 kgf = 9'8 N. 



Printed at Neelkamal Printers, Delhi, India
